139252.title: TransportGetTransformStatsAction can eat a transport thread, causing cluster instability
139252.description:
Transform stats does a fair bit of work just sitting in direct executor. This is not good. Depending on the scale of the cluster, if multiple users call the stats call for transforms, it could disconnect node from a cluster.

We should:

Make this way way cheaper, only consider transform tasks (do filtering directly in tasks request, not after gathering all tasks on the node) and be careful about ginormous strings being created and concatenated
Consider moving this off of direct executor.
Some additional notes:

This is 100% a bug that needs reporting to the transform (ML?) folks. We seem to be looping over all tasks, filtering them by description (not even filtering by action first??). Building the description of a single search task might not be too costly but isn't exactly free either, and building a description of them all could be very expensive, and even worse I'm pretty sure no search tasks could possibly have a matching description anyway. Moreover this is all happening on the transport_worker for no good reason and needs to be moved elsewhere as a matter of some urgency.

113615.title: Elasticsearch accepts script processors that are strings and not map

128583.title: TransportIndicesStatsAction causes starvation of tasks on management thread pool due to Engine.getSparseVectorValueCount
128583.description:
Engine.getSparseVectorValueCount might block 100% of the management threads in case we're facing frequent cache misses.
This causes the thread pool to queue and potentially starve important other work that's also depending on the management thread pool.
This was discovered on an internal serverless project.

135472.title: GroupShardsIterator can significantly tie up transport workers
135472.description:
When querying many shards, it has been observed that iterating the shards themselves can end up tying up a transport_worker thread. I am not sure if we want to optimize this path further or pivot to a different thread when above some shard threshold.

Switching to another threadpool on few shards (<10k?) seems unhelpful.

134925.title: Transforms will infinitely queue PIT closures causing a "PIT storm"
134925.description:
Transforms when using point-in-time (PIT) search will create multiple PITs over the lifetime of a single transform pivot page.

If there is any failure, or a new search is initiated, or the scheduled pivot completes, it will request the PITs to be deleted.

However, it will not wait for these PITs to be deleted before scheduling again or continuing with another set of searches. Consequently, its possible for many transforms, in quick succession, could create MANY PITs and cause a significant queue of close pit requests which can cause pressure on the system.

Transforms should wait for all its close-pit requests to complete before continuing its execution paths. Since close-pit "should" be fast, this should be OK. However, if close pit is slow, we want transforms to be naturally throttled to prevent a PIT storm.

105065.title: Avoid race in LocalHealthMonitor w.r.t null values
105065.description:
There is a race condition in the LocalHealthMonitor regarding null values (i.e. initial/reset values):

Last reported value was null
there is new a health node
New run starts the update process and records previous value null
health node/master change
new reported value is null
Run sees null and considers that it's ok to update the value....
Can probably relatively easily be fixed by using some form of ref counting/versioning of the lastReportedValue
